=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 262-271, function _shell_segments_with_operators | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: When parsing shell redirections such as 2>&1, the code treats > as the redirect operator, pop the preceding digit 2 from segment, and sets redirect_target True. On the next token &, redirect_target is True so the code resets redirect_target to False and continues. The subsequent token 1 (the file descriptor that is the actual redirect target) is never consumed as a redirect target and is appended to segment as a positional argument. In the context of a git push command being guard-checked, this spilled 1 is parsed as an extra refspec in _push_targets, where it resolves to a branch name or an unresolvable target that then checks the checkout branch. The same spill occurs for 2>&- (close fd 2) where - leaks as a positional argument.
  WHY: A git push origin HEAD:feature/open 2>&1 typed in the session is parsed with 1 as an extra push refspec. If the current checkout branch is merged, the guard blocks the push with exit code 2 because it checks the merged branch, even though the user's explicit target is an open branch. This is a regression introduced by the LAST RUN DIFF redirect-handling addition; the pre-existing code without redirect support did not spill tokens at all. The fix is: when redirect_target is True and token is &, keep redirect_target True instead of resetting it, so the token after & (the actual file descriptor) is consumed as the redirect target.

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 262-274 in _shell_segments_with_operators (the new redirect_target branch) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The new `redirect_target` skip branch in `_shell_segments_with_operators()` consumes the `&` in a `2>&1` file-descriptor redirection but resets the flag before the trailing digit is examined, so `1` is appended to a fresh segment as a command argument. For the common shell idiom `git push origin HEAD:feature/open 2>&1`, the parser now produces an extra `("&", ["1"])` segment alongside the real push command; in `_push_targets()` the literal `1` is treated as a positional refspec; in `_evaluate_bash()` the resulting `target.tip="1"` is fed to `git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options 1^{commit}`, which fails and the guard falls back to checking the current checkout branch.
  WHY: A push from a workspace whose checked-out branch is already merged (or whose branch resolves to anything other than the user-supplied refspec) will be blocked by the guard's spurious second refspec instead of being permitted, because the leaked `"1"` token resolves against and re-checks the wrong target. The same shape breaks `cmd > file 2>&1`, `cmd &> file`, and any `<&N` / `>&N` redirection. The fix needs to either (a) skip both the `&` and the following fd-digit as a single redirect-target pair, or (b) match the `&` as a redirect-opener that consumes the next fd-digit only when that token is purely digits — i.e. `if redirect_target and token.isdigit(): redirect_target = False; continue` rather than resetting on the `&` itself.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 348-360 in _guarded_git_invocations, the new `+=` environment assignment handling | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The strip-`+` branch (`name = name[:-1]`) drops the `+` but then unconditionally sets `working_directory = None` when the stripped name is `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_WORK_TREE`. The intent is "appending to a Git override is shell-state-dependent so we cannot trust the captured value", and the right behaviour is indeed to drop the working-directory override — but the same fall-through silently also *removes* the in-progress `environment` entry that is about to be populated one line later (`environment[name] = value`). Because the `if name in ("GIT_DIR", "GIT_WORK_TREE")` check immediately below runs against the stripped `name`, `environment[name] = value` still records the new value. However, when the user writes `GIT_DIR+=` and the resulting `GIT_DIR` is *not* recorded (e.g. the test suite only writes the append form once, the captured value is meaningless), the guard still considers the working directory authoritative even though the resolved GIT_DIR could be from the inherited shell state — the guard is one branch too lenient.
  WHY: A command of the shape `GIT_DIR+=value git ...` in a Bash tool call from a host process whose inherited GIT_DIR is outside the session checkout will pass the guard with `working_directory = None` (correctly rejecting the override), but the captured `environment["GIT_DIR"]` reflects only the appended suffix concatenated onto the inherited value, so the guard's later `git rev-parse --verify` runs in a checkout the host did not authorise. The fix is to also `continue` past the `environment[name] = value` write when the assignment was an append form, mirroring the "we don't trust the captured value" decision. Minor compared to the redirect bug above; flag as defensive.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 1306-1320 in _evaluate_bash | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The new `target = target._replace(tip=resolved_source_sha.strip())` path runs only when `code == 0` AND `target.tip != "HEAD"`. But for the `2>&1` failure mode (see CORRECTNESS finding above), the leaked `"1"` resolves against the host shell's cwd, returns 0 with a SHA, and the guard silently re-targets the actual push to that SHA — bypassing the merged-PR protection the guard exists to enforce. The guard now has two separate "trust the captured value" code paths and the `_replace` is one of them; the absence of a "this tip came from an unexpected source path, fail closed" check means a malformed command silently succeeds against the wrong ref.
  WHY: Combined with the redirect bug, a user-issued `git push origin HEAD:open-branch 2>&1` from a workspace whose current branch is merged will be guarded with `target.tip = "1"`'s resolution (some other commit on disk), the `_replace` accepts that resolved SHA, and the subsequent branch check passes — but the push itself then either silently no-ops (because `1^{commit}` is not a valid ref) or is permitted against the wrong refspec. The fail-closed posture requires an explicit "tip was user-supplied, not auto-resolved" check before `_replace` is allowed.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: the entire _shell_segments_with_operators rewrite (LAST RUN DIFF lines 262-274) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The merge-status guard is the pre-push safety net for every Bash tool invocation; the new redirection handling was added without a paired test fixture that exercises the `2>&1` / `>&2` / `&>` / `<&N` cases the parser is supposed to skip. The current test surface (per the LAST RUN CHANGED FILES scope and the symbol-diff summary) did not grow a regression for this path.
